title: Nonthaburi Riverside Cycling: 2-Day Ko Kret Plan | ThailandAddict
metaDesc: A 2-day Nonthaburi cycling plan along the Chao Phraya in Thailand: warm up at Suan Somdet Park in Pak Kret, then loop Ko Kret island, with bike rental spots, prices, hours, and real food stops.
keywords: Nonthaburi cycling, Suan Somdet Park Nonthaburi, Ko Kret cycling, Chao Phraya riverside bike route
intro: Nonthaburi is easier to cycle than most people expect. You get a shady public park with a riding loop around a lake, plus Ko Kret, an island in the middle of the Chao Phraya River that you can ride all the way around in about 6 km. This is a 2-day plan for anyone who wants a relaxed riverside ride without being super fit, with plenty of good food stops along the way.

blocks.html: If you want to cycle near Bangkok without dealing with heavy traffic, Nonthaburi is the answer most people overlook. The Pak Kret side has Suan Somdet Phra Sri Nakharin (Suan Somdet Park), with a riding loop around a big pond shaded by mature trees. Ko Kret, meanwhile, is an island in the river where cars can't go, so you can ride the whole island with peace of mind. We've laid this out as a 2-day plan: warm up in the park on day one, then take the ferry over to tackle the island on day two.

items: Day 1 — Suan Somdet Park + the Pak Kret riverside Ride in the park in the morning, then cruise along to catch the Rama V Bridge view in the evening.
Day 2 — Loop around Ko Kret Take the ferry across, rent a bike at Wat Poramai Yikawat, ride the 6 km loop, and stop by the market and the Mon temples.
Difficulty Easy to moderate, almost all flat, good for beginners and families.
What to bring Helmet, drinking water, sunscreen, and cash (the ferry and bike rentals are cash only).

blocks.title: Best Time to Go
blocks.html: Ride in the morning from 6:00–9:00 or in the evening from 16:30 onward to avoid the harsh sun. Suan Somdet Park opens around 5 a.m. Ko Kret gets crowded on Saturdays and Sundays, so if you want the road to yourself, try a weekday.

items.note: Out and back in a day

blocks.text: Day 1 — Suan Somdet Park and the Pak Kret Riverside

blocks.html: Suan Somdet Phra Sri Nakharin in Nonthaburi is in Pak Kret district, an older public park that locals usually just call Suan Somdet Ya. It's been renovated and has a running track and a bike lane along a large pond full of fish. Entry is free, and it's a good place to warm up on day one before you tackle the island.

blocks.label: Day 1
blocks.title: Warm up in the park + riverside views

items.activity: Enter Suan Somdet Park, Pak Kret
items.note: Open roughly 05:00–20:00, free entry. The morning air is still cool and pleasant.
Flat, plenty of shade, with rest spots and restrooms. Good for warming up your legs before the real trip.
There are several rice-porridge and coffee shops along Chaeng Watthana and Tiwanon roads.

items.activity: Cruise along the Pak Kret embankment, take in the Rama V Bridge view
items.note: The evening light is soft and great for photos, with a wide view of the Chao Phraya.

items.activity: Dinner at a riverside spot in Pak Kret
items.note: There are several restaurants with river views near the Pak Kret pier.

blocks.title: About the Bikes
blocks.html: If you don't have your own bike for day one, you can drive or ride a motorbike over, park, and just walk or jog in the park. The park itself doesn't have a regular bike rental stand, and most people bring their own. Save the serious bike rental for day two on Ko Kret.

The highlight of the trip is here. Ko Kret is an island in the middle of the Chao Phraya River where cars can't go, with narrow concrete paths that loop around the island for about 6 km. Along the way you pass Mon temples, a pottery-making community, Mon dessert shops, and river viewpoints. Ride at a relaxed pace, stop to eat as you go, and you can easily spend a half day here.

To get to the island, take the cross-river ferry from the Wat Sanam Nuea pier in Pak Kret; the fare is just a few baht per person. Once you reach the island side in front of Wat Poramai Yikawat, you'll find bike rental shops to choose from. Plain city bikes start at around 40–50 THB per day with no time limit. If your legs aren't up for it, there are e-bikes for rent too, charged by the hour at around 150 THB.

blocks.label: Day 2
blocks.title: Ferry across – rent a bike – loop the island

items.activity: Arrive at Wat Sanam Nuea pier, Pak Kret
items.note: Take the ferry over to Ko Kret; the fare is just a few baht per person. Go early while it's still quiet.

items.activity: Rent a bike in front of Wat Poramai Yikawat
items.note: City bikes around 40–50 THB/day, e-bikes around 150 THB/hr. Check the tires and brakes before you set off.

items.activity: Pay respects at Wat Poramai Yikawat
items.note: An old Mon temple with a leaning riverside pagoda that's a symbol of the island.

items.activity: Start the 6 km loop around the island
items.note: Narrow concrete path, a one-way loop so it's hard to get lost, passing gardens, Mon houses, and riverside fields.

items.activity: Stop by the Mon pottery community + dessert shops
items.note: Try the fried fish cakes with bamboo shoots, khao chae (chilled rice), and Mon sweets at the community shops.

items.activity: Head back to the market by the temple for lunch
items.note: The Ko Kret market is busiest on Saturdays and Sundays, with lots of food.

items.activity: Return the bike, take the ferry back to Pak Kret
items.note: Allow time for the hot afternoon sun and head back at an easy pace.

items.name: Bike rental in front of Wat Poramai Yikawat (Ko Kret)
items.blurb: The main rental point as soon as you step off the ferry, with city bikes in several sizes, good for looping the island. It's the most popular because it sits right at the island's entrance.

items.name: E-bike rental, Ko Kret
items.blurb: Electric bikes for rent for anyone who doesn't want to work too hard, or who's bringing older relatives along, making the island loop easier. Charged by the hour or as a flat rate by agreement.

items.name: Bring your own bike (Suan Somdet Park, Pak Kret)
items.blurb: For day one at Suan Somdet Park, most people bring their own bike. The park has no regular rental stand, but there's a free riding loop around the pond.

items.name: Ko Kret Market (by Wat Poramai)
items.blurb: Mon food and street eats: fried fish cakes with bamboo shoots, khao chae, and old-school Thai sweets. Busiest on weekends.

items.name: Mon dessert shops in the community
items.blurb: As you ride you'll pass Mon snack and dessert shops along the way. Worth stopping in to taste a few here and there.

items.name: Riverside spots at Pak Kret pier
items.blurb: On the Pak Kret side there are restaurants with Chao Phraya River views, good for dinner to wrap up day one.

blocks.text: Tips for a Fun, Safe Ride

items: Check the bike before you go — tire pressure and brakes matter most, especially on rental bikes that lots of people use one after another.
Carry cash — the ferry fare and bike rentals are mostly cash only, and many of the small shops on the island don't take transfers.
The island paths are narrow — ride slowly, watch for pedestrians and spots where paths cross in front of houses, and use a bell or slow down instead of honking.
Avoid the midday sun — both the park and the island have patches of shade, but 11:00–15:00 is genuinely hot, so morning or evening is better.
Weekends get busy — Ko Kret is lively on Saturdays and Sundays but also packed. If you want an open road, go on a weekday.

faq.q: What are the hours for Suan Somdet Park in Nonthaburi, and can you cycle there?
faq.a: It's open roughly 05:00–20:00 daily, with free entry. There's a bike lane along a large pond that's easy to ride, but the park itself has no regular bike rental stand, so most people bring their own. It's great for warming up in the morning or evening.

faq.q: How long is the cycling loop around Ko Kret?
faq.a: The loop around Ko Kret is about 6 km on a narrow, flat concrete path. It's a one-way loop, so it's hard to get lost, and you can ride at a relaxed pace, stopping to eat and take photos. It easily fills a half day.

faq.q: How much does it cost to rent a bike on Ko Kret, and where?
faq.a: There are bike rental shops in front of Wat Poramai Yikawat, right as you step off the ferry. Plain city bikes start at around 40–50 THB per day with no time limit, and e-bikes are available too, charged by the hour at around 150 THB. Bring cash.

faq.q: How do you take the ferry to Ko Kret?
faq.a: Take the cross-river ferry from the Wat Sanam Nuea pier in Pak Kret; the fare is just a few baht per person. You land in front of Wat Poramai Yikawat, which is exactly where the bike rentals are and where the island loop begins.

faq.q: Is this 2-day cycling plan good for beginners?
faq.a: Yes. Both Suan Somdet Park and Ko Kret are almost entirely flat, the distances aren't long, and you can ride slowly, so it suits beginners and families. Just avoid the midday sun and check your bike before setting off.
